institution: SAE Institute Spain — Madrid & Barcelona; título awarded by UDIMA
programme_name: Máster en Producción de Música Urbana
city: Madrid AND Barcelona — the same programme is taught on both SAE campuses, with different start dates per campus (Madrid: Febrero 2026 / Octubre 2026; Barcelona: Octubre 2026 / Febrero de 2027)
autonomous_community: Comunidad de Madrid (Madrid campus) AND Cataluña / Catalunya (Barcelona campus). The awarding university, UDIMA, is seated in Collado Villalba, Comunidad de Madrid
campus: SAE Institute Madrid and SAE Institute Barcelona — SAE's own page lists 'Campus: Madrid, Barcelona' for this programme. Teaching is face-to-face in SAE's own studios; UDIMA does not teach it
university_awarding: Universidad a Distancia de Madrid (UDIMA) — SAE's page states the qualification is 'otorgado por la Universidad a Distancia de Madrid, UDIMA' and 'acreditado por UDIMA'. SAE Institute itself is not a university and awards only its own 'Diploma Profesional de SAE'. CONFLICT on the fallback award: the programme page says the non-graduate route yields a 'Máster Profesional emitido por UDIMA', while SAE's own press release on the UDIMA agreement says that route yields a 'Máster Profesional emitido por SAE Creative Media Institute España'. Both recorded
institution_type: private school (not a university) — SAE Institute Spain, part of SAE Creative Media Education. The awarding body UDIMA is a private university (Ley 1/2006, de 14 de junio, de Reconocimiento de la Universidad Privada «Universidad a Distancia de Madrid» (UDIMA), BOCM 28/06/2006, BOE 09/08/2006). Note SAE Barcelona is separately an authorised centre for some official titles, but THIS programme is not one of them
official_status: título propio — specifically marketed as 'Máster en Formación Permanente en Producción de Música Urbana acreditado por UDIMA (25 ECTS)'. Máster de Formación Permanente is the post-RD 822/2021 legal name for a título propio: NOT ANECA-verified, NOT an official máster universitario, not in the official register of official titles. FURTHER PROBLEM WITH THE NAME ITSELF: RD 822/2021 art. 37.6 defines 'el Máster de Formación Permanente (con una carga de 60, 90 y 120 créditos ECTS), el Diploma de Especialización (con entre 30 y 59 créditos) y el Diploma de Experto (de menos de 30 créditos)', and art. 37.9 reserves the denomination 'Máster de Formación Permanente'. At 25 ECTS this award falls in the Diploma de Experto band and carries less than half the minimum credit load the regulation sets for anything called a Máster de Formación Permanente. Flagged CONFLICT between SAE/UDIMA's naming and RD 822/2021
boe_order: None for this qualification. The only BOE references here are (a) RD 822/2021 art. 37, the rule the 25-ECTS 'máster' naming fails, and (b) BOE 09/08/2006 recognising UDIMA itself as a private university — which is about the institution, not about this title
meces_level: NOT IN MECES — a título propio / formación permanente award is outside the Marco Español de Cualificaciones para la Educación Superior
eqf_level: NOT IN EQF — no MECES level means no mapped EQF level. Any '25 ECTS' figure on the page is a workload count, not a framework level
europe_recognition: NO AUTOMATIC EUROPEAN RECOGNITION. This is a título propio (Máster de Formación Permanente) awarded by UDIMA, not a máster universitario. It is not in MECES, not inside the EHEA/Bologna qualifications framework, carries no Diploma Supplement as of right, and grants no doctoral access. There is no automatic academic recognition in any other European country: recognition is entirely at the discretion of the receiving institution or employer. AND THE CREDIT COUNT MAKES IT WORSE, NOT MARGINAL: at 25 ECTS this is roughly a third of the smallest official second-cycle master (60 ECTS). A 25-ECTS award is NOT a second-cycle qualification under any reading — not under MECES, not under the EHEA (a Bologna second cycle is 60-120 ECTS), and not even under Spain's own títulos-propios naming rule in RD 822/2021 art. 37.6, where 25 ECTS is a Diploma de Experto. SAE's press release describes UDIMA as 'universidad plenamente reconocida en el Espacio Europeo de Educación Superior' — that statement is about UDIMA the institution and provides NO legal basis for recognition of this particular non-official award. Do not read it as one
tuition_eu_eur: NOT FOUND — SAE publishes no price for this programme. The programme page has no fee figure; SAE's 'Becas y Ayudas' page quotes only percentage discounts ('60% descuento sobre el precio de la matrícula', '40% de descuento sobre el precio de la matrícula', etc.) against an unpublished base price. Price is disclosed only through the Admission Pack (formulario de inscripción, convenio de matriculación, Offer Letter, Plan de Pagos, domiciliación mensual). No primary-source figure exists to record
tuition_non_eu_eur: NOT FOUND — no price is published for any applicant category, so no non-EU differential can be confirmed or denied. Page silence, not evidence of 'no surcharge'. As a private school SAE would ordinarily charge one flat rate, but that is not stated on the page and is therefore not recorded as a finding
fees_extra_eur: NOT FOUND — no enrolment, insurance or admin fee is published. Non-EU applicants must additionally obtain a Spanish student visa / autorización de estancia por estudios ('si no eres de un país miembro de la Unión Europea deberás de tramitar una autorización o visado de estancia por estudios'), whose costs are borne by the applicant and are not published here
modality: presencial (face-to-face) at the Madrid or Barcelona campus. Duration 8 months
language_of_instruction: Español (Spanish) — stated explicitly under both the national and the international entry-requirements tabs: 'IDIOMA: Español', and for international students 'Para estudiar en SAE, requerimos evidenciar su capacidad para hablar, escuchar, leer y escribir en castellano'. NO English track. This is a hard filter for a candidate at Spanish A0/A1
start_month: February and October. Madrid: Febrero 2026, Octubre 2026. Barcelona: Octubre 2026, Febrero de 2027. Spring (February) intake CONFIRMED. No February 2027 Madrid date and no 2027-28 calendar published at access date
notes: ECTS ESTABLISHED: 25 ECTS, stated twice on SAE's own page ('Máster en Formación Permanente en Producción de Música Urbana acreditado por UDIMA (25 ECTS)' and 'el Máster de Formación Permanente (25 ECTS), o Máster Profesional, otorgado por la Universidad a Distancia de Madrid, UDIMA'), and consistent with SAE's press release stating the four SAE-UDIMA masters carry 'una carga lectiva que oscila entre 25 y 60 ECTS, según el programa elegido'. AWARDING BODY ESTABLISHED: UDIMA (private university), not SAE; SAE awards only its own Diploma Profesional, which is not a university qualification at all. TWO AWARDS, TWO ROUTES: applicants who already hold an official university degree get the 25-ECTS Máster de Formación Permanente from UDIMA; applicants without one get a 'Máster Profesional' (page says emitted by UDIMA, press release says emitted by SAE — CONFLICT logged) on the strength of 2 years' professional experience. This candidate (300-ECTS Tunisian Software Engineering degree) would qualify for the first route, subject to SAE accepting a foreign title as 'título universitario oficial de Grado ... o equivalente'. FOR THIS CANDIDATE SPECIFICALLY: a 25-ECTS título propio does not deliver a second-cycle qualification, PhD access, public-scholarship eligibility, or automatic recognition anywhere in the EHEA; and under RD 822/2021 art. 4/art. 5 credits from non-official studies count towards an official Spanish degree only up to 15% of that degree's plan, so it is not a stepping stone into an official master either. Also note the register point: RD 822/2021 art. 37.11 lets a university request RUCT inclusion of a genuine Máster de Formación Permanente, so even a future RUCT row for such a title would NOT make it official — do not read RUCT presence as officiality for formación permanente. ADMISSION: entrevista de acceso plus admission questionnaire; +18 for international students. VISA: SAE's press release claims 'las titulaciones permiten acceder al visado de estudiante para alumnos internacionales' — recorded as SAE's claim, not verified against Spanish immigration rules here.

Even setting aside its non-official status, 30 ECTS is half the minimum load of any second-cycle master — a Bologna second cycle is 60-120 ECTS, and Spain's own títulos-propios scale in RD 822/2021 art. 37.6 puts 30-59 ECTS in the 'Diploma de Especialización' band, reserving the name 'Máster de Formación Permanente' for 60/90/120 ECTS. So this is NOT a master's-level qualification by credit volume either, whatever any marketing elsewhere may call it. UFV is honest here: its own page calls it a Postgrado and a Título Propio, and the word 'Máster' appears on the page only in the navigation list of OTHER UFV programmes

This is a 30-ECTS postgrado, NOT a master at all, and no wording anywhere may override that credit count. In fact UFV does not call it a master: the <title>, the H1 and the breadcrumb all say 'Postgrado', the Titulación box says 'Título Propio', and the assessed piece is a 'TFP' (Trabajo Fin de Postgrado), not a TFM. FOR THIS CANDIDATE: 30 ECTS of non-official credit gives no PhD access, no public-scholarship eligibility, and under RD 822/2021 credits from non-official studies count towards an official Spanish degree only up to 15% of that degree's plan — so it is not a bridge into an official master either. INDUSTRY VALUE IS THE ONLY REAL CASE FOR IT: delivered 'En colaboración con Warner Music', with 'prácticas garantizadas', an academic director who is the former president of Warner Music Spain & Portugal and Warner Music México, and a faculty of working industry professionals.
